stem: Best guess: which procedure best detects sales recorded before goods were shipped?

choices.text: Tracing shipping documents to recorded sales invoices
Recomputing the allowance for credit losses at year-end
Comparing year-end invoice dates with shipping dates
Confirming year-end cash balances with the bank

explanation: Cut-off tests compare recording dates with the date control transferred (usually shipment).

stem: Which procedure best tests the **completeness** of sales?

choices.text: Vouch recorded sales to shipping documents
Review the adequacy of the allowance account
Confirm receivable balances with customers
Trace shipping documents to recorded sales
choices.explanation: Correct. Completeness: trace from source documents (shipping records) into the accounting records.

explanation: Completeness: trace from source documents (shipping records) into the accounting records.

stem: The auditor decides not to confirm receivables because customers are government agencies known not to respond. What is required?

choices.text: Document why confirmation was skipped; do other procedures
choices.explanation: Correct. AU-C 330: if the auditor doesn't confirm receivables, it documents the basis (immaterial, ineffective, or low RMM with other procedures).

choices.text: Nothing, because confirmation of receivables is optional
choices.explanation: Confirmation is presumed; the decision must be documented.

choices.text: Qualify the opinion for a scope limitation on receivables
choices.explanation: Not if sufficient evidence is obtained another way.

choices.text: Send negative confirmation requests to the agencies instead
choices.explanation: Negative confirmations would also be ineffective here.

explanation: AU-C 330: if the auditor doesn't confirm receivables, it documents the basis (immaterial, ineffective, or low RMM with other procedures).

stem: A company recorded a $500,000 sale on December 30 for goods shipped January 3 under FOB shipping point terms. What is the misstatement at December 31?

choices.text: None, because the invoice was dated and sent in December
choices.explanation: Revenue is recognized when control transfers, not when invoiced.

choices.text: Revenue and receivables are understated by $500,000
choices.explanation: It was recorded too early, not omitted.

choices.text: Revenue and receivables are overstated by $500,000
choices.explanation: Correct. Under FOB shipping point, control transfers at shipment (January 3).

choices.text: Only a disclosure of the January shipment is needed
choices.explanation: This is a cut-off error requiring adjustment if material.

explanation: Under FOB shipping point, control transfers at shipment (January 3). Recording in December overstates revenue and receivables.

stem: Which procedure is most effective at detecting side agreements that give customers a right of return?

choices.text: Recomputing the totals on sales invoices
Reviewing the receivables aging report
Tracing shipping documents to sales invoices
Confirming key sales terms with customers
choices.explanation: Correct. Confirming terms (not just balances) and reading contracts helps identify side agreements that affect revenue recognition.

explanation: Confirming terms (not just balances) and reading contracts helps identify side agreements that affect revenue recognition.

stem: Which situation best supports overcoming the presumption to confirm receivables?

choices.text: Receivables are immaterial to the financial statements
choices.explanation: Correct. Exceptions: immaterial balance, confirmation ineffective, or low RMM with other substantive procedures that address it.

choices.text: Receivables are material and RMM is high
The client prefers that customers not be contacted
choices.explanation: Client preference alone doesn't overcome the presumption.

choices.text: The auditor is short of time
choices.explanation: Time pressure doesn't overcome the presumption.

explanation: Exceptions: immaterial balance, confirmation ineffective, or low RMM with other substantive procedures that address it.

stem: A cashier steals Customer A's payment and later applies Customer B's payment to A's account. What is this scheme, and what detects it?

choices.text: Kiting; detected by a schedule of bank transfers
Channel stuffing; detected by distributor sales analytics
Lapping; compare deposit slips to postings, confirm balances
Bill-and-hold; detected by observing warehouse inventory

explanation: Lapping delays postings. Comparing remittance details on deposit slips to postings and confirming balances can reveal it.

stem: Unusually large credit memos were issued in January for December sales to one distributor. What does this most likely indicate?

choices.text: Strong customer service during the holiday season
choices.explanation: Large post-year-end credits for year-end sales signal a problem.

choices.text: An inventory valuation problem at the distributor only
Understatement of December revenue from that distributor
Possible December revenue overstatement or channel stuffing
choices.explanation: Correct. Post-year-end returns and credits for year-end sales are a classic sign of improper revenue recognition.

explanation: Post-year-end returns and credits for year-end sales are a classic sign of improper revenue recognition.

stem: Which procedure best tests the valuation of receivables?

choices.text: Test later cash receipts on year-end balances; evaluate aging
choices.explanation: Correct. Subsequent collections and aging analysis bear directly on collectibility (net realizable value).

choices.text: Vouching recorded sales to shipping documents
Tracing shipping documents to sales invoices
Reading the board minutes for pledged receivables

explanation: Subsequent collections and aging analysis bear directly on collectibility (net realizable value).

stem: Which revenue red flag is most consistent with fictitious sales?

choices.text: Days sales outstanding falling from 50 to 40 days
choices.explanation: Faster collection doesn't suggest fictitious sales.

choices.text: Receivables outgrowing sales, from new customers with no history
choices.explanation: Correct. Fictitious sales leave uncollected receivables and often involve unfamiliar customers.

choices.text: Stable gross margins that are in line with the industry
A decrease in sales returns and allowances
choices.explanation: Fewer returns isn't a typical fictitious-sales indicator.

explanation: Fictitious sales leave uncollected receivables and often involve unfamiliar customers.

stem: Goods under a bill-and-hold arrangement are still in the seller's warehouse at year-end. What should the auditor evaluate before accepting the revenue?

choices.text: Only whether the invoice was sent to the customer
Whether all bill-and-hold criteria for revenue are met
choices.explanation: Correct. ASC 606 bill-and-hold criteria must all be met for revenue before physical delivery; the auditor tests them.

choices.text: Whether the customer paid a deposit on the goods
Nothing more, if the customer confirms the receivable balance
choices.explanation: Balance confirmation doesn't establish the criteria.

explanation: ASC 606 bill-and-hold criteria must all be met for revenue before physical delivery; the auditor tests them.

stem: Shipped December 30 under FOB destination and delivered January 4; the sale was recorded December 30. What is the effect on December 31 statements?

choices.text: No effect, because the goods had shipped
choices.explanation: Control passes on delivery under FOB destination.

choices.text: Revenue is overstated; the sale belongs to January
choices.explanation: Correct. FOB destination: control passes at delivery (January 4), so December revenue is overstated and inventory understated.

choices.text: Revenue is understated for December
Inventory is overstated at year-end
choices.explanation: Inventory was removed early, so it is understated.

explanation: FOB destination: control passes at delivery (January 4), so December revenue is overstated and inventory understated.

stem: Which procedure addresses the **presentation** assertion for receivables?

choices.text: Confirming receivable balances with customers
Reading loan agreements for pledged receivables
choices.explanation: Correct. Pledges, factoring, related-party receivables, and concentrations require appropriate disclosure.

choices.text: Recomputing invoice totals and extensions
Tracing shipping documents to recorded sales

explanation: Pledges, factoring, related-party receivables, and concentrations require appropriate disclosure.
